mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE < 5.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5 percentage points and 100,000 persons respectively over one month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.5pp AND PAYEMS falls > 100000 in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both UNRATE and PAYEMS deteriorate by the specified thresholds in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio) above their respective 12-month averages for three consecutive months signals a recovery in household demand, which boosts consumption and corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month avg AND RSAFS/GDPC1 > 12-month avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both HOUST and the savings rate proxy exceed their 12-month averages for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance by the Fed, which rapidly raises borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) after a >0.75pp single-month FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent inversion of the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months, combined with a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below its 12-month average, signals both supply weakness and falling inflation, which together reduce cost pressures but also indicate weak demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month MA for 4 months AND CPIAUCSL < 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO is below its 6-month MA for four months and CPIAUCSL is below its 12-month average.
